channel.title: HushBook Blog
channel.description: Guides to immersive reading and read-along audiobooks.

item.title: How to Read Classics Without Getting Bored: Why They Feel Hard and Where to Start
item.description: Boredom with a classic usually means the reading is too hard or feels pointless. Why classics feel hard, ways to stay with one, six short classics to start with, and how to read and hear them free.

item.title: How to Put Audiobooks on iPhone: From a PC, a Mac or Without iTunes
item.description: Audiobooks from Apple Books, Audible or Libby download in their own app. For your own MP3 or M4B files: iCloud Drive or a USB drive from a PC, Finder sync or AirDrop from a Mac, or Safari on the phone. Plus where audiobooks go.

item.title: Can You Read Along With Spotify Audiobooks? Page Match, Recaps and Transcripts
item.description: Not on screen: Spotify shows no text while an audiobook plays. What Page Match, Recaps and Follow-Along do, how to read along with your own copy of the book, which Spotify podcasts have transcripts, and a word-by-word option.

item.title: How to Keep Track of Characters in a Book or Audiobook
item.description: Keep a running cast list: each new name, a few words on who they are, and one tie to someone you know. Methods for print, ebooks and audiobooks, why listening makes it harder, and how to handle War and Peace.

item.title: Can Libby Read to You? Read Aloud, Read-Alongs and Audiobooks
item.description: Not by itself: Libby has no read-aloud button. It lends audiobooks and narrated read-alongs for kids, and works with VoiceOver and TalkBack. How to set up each one, and how to read along with a Libby audiobook anyway.

item.title: Is LibriVox Safe, Legal and Free? What to Know Before You Download
item.description: Yes. LibriVox is a free, ad-free volunteer project, and every book it records is public domain in the US. Outside the US, check the book first. What to know about safety, copyright, AI narration, quality and unofficial apps.

item.title: Does Reading Along With an Audiobook Help? What the Research Says
item.description: Yes, when listening alone would lose you: dense books, a new language, struggling readers or a wandering mind. For a confident reader it adds little, and the narrator can slow you down. What the studies show, and how to do it well.

item.title: Are Audiobooks Good for Kids? What the Research Says
item.description: Yes, for most school-age children, as an addition to reading together. Audiobooks build vocabulary and story comprehension, and the gains are biggest when kids see the words. What studies show for toddlers, new readers and audio vs TV.

item.title: How to Retain Information From Audiobooks: 8 Habits Backed by Research
item.description: Audiobooks are not a weaker way to learn, but listening lets your mind drift. Recall after each chapter, spaced sessions, reading along on dense books and the right speed help you remember more, with the studies behind each habit.

item.title: Are Audiobooks Good for ADHD? What the Research Actually Shows
item.description: For many people with ADHD, audiobooks make books easier to start and finish, and small studies link read-aloud tools to less distraction and fatigue. But listening does not bypass attention problems. The evidence, and tips that help.

item.title: How to Listen to Audiobooks for Free (Legally): 9 Ways That Work
item.description: Your library card unlocks free audiobooks in Libby and Hoopla. Without one, LibriVox has 21,000+ public domain titles and Audible has free listens. What each option gives you, the catch, and free services for print disabilities.

item.title: Are Audiobooks Good for Dyslexia? What the Research Says
item.description: Yes, as a companion to reading, not a replacement. Read-aloud tools modestly improve comprehension, and experts recommend following the words while listening. What the studies show for kids and adults, and whether dyslexia fonts help.

item.title: How Long Is an Audiobook? Hours for a 300-Page Book, and at 1.5x
item.description: A 300-page book runs about 8 to 10.5 hours. We counted the words in ten classics and compared them with their LibriVox recordings, from Alice at 2 hours 47 minutes to the King James Bible at 101 hours, plus 1.5x and 2x times.

item.title: How to Play M4B Files on iPhone, Android, Windows and Mac
item.description: Open M4B audiobooks in a player that keeps chapters and your place: Voice, VLC or Smart AudioBook Player on Android, BookPlayer or HushBook on iPhone, VLC on Windows, Apple Books on Mac. Plus why some M4B files will not play.

item.title: How to Learn English With Audiobooks (and Why Reading Along Helps)
item.description: Listen while you read the same words. Learners who read along could translate about eight times as many new words as those who only listened. What the research says, a daily routine, free English audiobooks, and books for each level.

item.title: Why Do I Fall Asleep Listening to Audiobooks? And Is It Bad?
item.description: A story gives your mind something to follow that is not your own worries, right when your body is primed to sleep. What a 2026 survey of 1,136 bedtime listeners found, whether the habit is bad, and how to keep your place.

item.title: How to Focus on Audiobooks When Your Mind Keeps Wandering
item.description: Listening gives your mind more room to drift than reading does, and a 2013 study shows it. Why it happens, seven fixes that work, and how reading along with the words keeps you on track.

item.title: What Speed Should You Listen to Audiobooks At?
item.description: Somewhere between 1x and 2x for most books. What the UCLA study on 2x playback found, where fast listening costs you, a speed guide by book type, and how to find your own speed.

item.title: What Is an Unabridged Audiobook? Abridged vs Unabridged Explained
item.description: Unabridged means the complete book read word for word. Abridged means an editor cut it first. What gets cut, why abridged editions exist, how to tell which one you are buying, and which to choose.

item.title: Free Read-Along Audiobooks: How to Read Along With Any Free Audiobook
item.description: Free audiobooks rarely come with synced text. Find free LibriVox and public domain audiobooks, then read along word by word with HushBook, which transcribes the audio on your phone.

item.title: Does Listening to an Audiobook Count as Reading?
item.description: Yes. Studies find comprehension from listening is about the same as from reading, and the brain processes meaning the same way. Where print still has an edge, where audio wins, and how to get both.

item.title: M4B vs MP3: Which Audiobook Format Should You Use?
item.description: M4B keeps a whole audiobook in one file with chapters and saved position. MP3 plays on almost anything. What each format is, how they compare on quality and chapters, and when to convert.

item.title: Can You Read Along With Audible? How Read & Listen Works
item.description: Yes, with Audible Read & Listen, if you own both the audiobook and the Kindle ebook. What you need, how to turn it on, what to do if you own one edition, and options for audiobooks that did not come from Audible.

item.title: What Is Immersive Reading? How to Read and Listen at the Same Time
item.description: Immersive reading means following the text while you listen to the audiobook. How it differs from text-to-speech and Microsoft Immersive Reader, and how to try it with HushBook on your own recording or a free public domain book.
